title: Wendell and the Rivergate
premise: Emrys Ishikawa, a storm chaser deep in debt to the Rivergate syndicate, takes a salvage contract to recover a vanished government survey team in the flood country around Lake Wendell. She finds one survivor, Wendell Okafor, who refuses to leave without the survey's sealed findings—evidence that the government engineered the flood to seize the valley. Pursued by both the syndicate and federal agents, Emrys must choose between paying her debts with the evidence and giving it to the displaced townsfolk. In the end she burns her debt ledger, delivers the truth publicly through Wendell's testimony, and finally stops running.
about_author: Bram Kavanagh is the pen name of a former river guide who spent a decade mapping floodplains across the American interior before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people whose loyalties cost more than their lives.

chapters.title: Debt of Weather
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Chasing a supercell across the plains to earn salvage money, she's intercepted by Rivergate collectors who give her one season to repay or forfeit her truck and freedom. A desperate contract arrives: find the missing Meridian Survey team near Lake Wendell. Emotional beat: cornered pragmatism masking dread.

chapters.title: The Quiet Valley
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She reaches the flooded valley and finds the survey camp intact—generators humming, coffee still warm, but no people and no tracks in the mud. Only a locked case stamped CLASSIFIED and a child's drawing pinned to a tent wall. Emotional beat: creeping wrongness; the silence is louder than any storm.

chapters.title: Wendell
chapters.summary: Wendell Okafor's POV. The lone survivor, a hydrologist hiding in an old church steeple, watches Emrys search and decides whether to trust her. He reveals the team scattered when they realized what the data showed—and that agents took the others 'for debriefing.' He won't leave without the case. Emotional beat: grief hardened into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Water Knows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wendell shows Emrys the survey readings: the levee was deliberately undersized to force evacuation and transfer the valley to federal hands. Emrys realizes the case is worth more than her life—and exactly what Rivergate would pay for it. Emotional beat: temptation arriving dressed as salvation.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Collectors
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Rivergate's enforcer, Sable Voss, tracks her down, offering to clear the debt if she hands over the case. Simultaneously, federal agent Corliss radios in, claiming Wendell is unstable and dangerous. Both offers are lies; Emrys can do the math. Emotional beat: the trap closing from two directions.

chapters.title: Running Water
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Fleeing through drowned backroads by airboat, Wendell and Emrys argue about justice: he wants public exposure, she wants survival first. An ambush by Corliss's team forces them into the flooded town of Rivergate itself, where displaced locals recognize Wendell. Emotional beat: loyalty forming under fire.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Hiding in the town's abandoned bank, Emrys finds Rivergate's own records—the syndicate profited from the same land grab, buying foreclosed farms at pennies. Her debt and the conspiracy share a spine. She photographs everything. Emotional beat: rage replacing fear; the personal becomes the political.

chapters.title: High Water Mark
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Voss corners them on the levee as a real storm bears down. Wendell chooses to stand and be seen rather than run, broadcasting the survey data over the emergency band while Emrys holds off Voss. Corliss arrives—not to arrest Wendell, but to silence everyone. Emotional beat: sacrifice as declaration.

chapters.title: Rivergate Rising
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Climax. In the storm's teeth, the townspeople—armed with Wendell's broadcast and Emrys's photos—surround the levee. Corliss's extraction team is exposed by its own radio traffic; Voss defects rather than drown for the syndicate. Emrys burns her debt ledger in front of witnesses. Emotional beat: catharsis; the current turns.

chapters.title: Where the River Ends
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Weeks later, hearings begin; the valley's families file claims with the evidence intact. Wendell rebuilds the survey station as a public archive. Emrys, debt-free and unburdened, loads her truck—but this time she pauses at the town limit, deciding where to go instead of fleeing somewhere. Emotional beat: stillness earned; stopping no longer costs more.
